results.name: A valid cigar+beverage request succeeds
A recommendation has an explanation (never unexplained)
A recommendation has a rule set version
A recommendation has a serving sequence
A recommendation has an alternative recommendation
A Full cigar against Whiskey (both intensity 4) reports an even intensity match
A Mild cigar against Whiskey (intensity 1 vs 4) reports a mismatched intensity, not falsely "even"
The mismatch produces a real conflict explanation
Selected notes that clash with the pairing type are flagged as a real conflict
A clashing pairing scores lower than a harmonious one
A request with no pairing type is rejected (400), never silently scored
A request with almost no real signal reports a real, non-fabricated confidence value below 1.0
Identical input produces an identical score on repeated requests (deterministic, not random)
Identical input produces an identical rule set version on repeated requests
A client-submitted compatScore/ruleSetVersion is silently ignored — the server always recomputes its own
A save request succeeds (201)
The saved score matches the server-computed score, never a client value
The save is visible in the caller's own saved-pairings list on reload
Fetching a single saved pairing returns its revision history
Re-saving with the same idempotency key does not duplicate — reports alreadySaved
The saved-pairings list still has exactly one row for this exact cigar+beverage combination
A rating update with the correct expectedVersion succeeds
Re-using the now-stale expectedVersion is rejected with a real 409 conflict, not silently overwritten
The rejected stale write never actually changed the rating
Each successful rating update appended a new revision row (real history, not overwritten in place)
A completely separate guest cannot read another guest's saved pairing (404, not 403 — existence is not leaked either)
A completely separate guest cannot rate another guest's saved pairing
A completely separate guest's own saved-pairings list never includes another guest's row
Guest-to-account conversion succeeds
Conversion reports the saved pairing was transferred (real found-and-verified requirement)
The saved pairing is visible under the new account identity
Two independent live fetches under the same identity return identical saved-pairing data (no per-device drift)
Rank returns every real pairing category
Rank results are sorted descending by score
Every ranked result has an explanation and rule version
A genuinely first-ever request from a fresh browser does not 401 (guest identity auto-issued)
